data.gender_notes: Gilles is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old French word gisil, meaning pledge, hostage, or servant. In medieval Europe, the name was often given to children born to noble families as a sign of good faith in a treaty or agreement. Gilles de Rais, a 15th-century French nobleman and military leader, was the most famous bearer of this name. The name Gilles carries the meaning “Pledge, hostage, servant” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Gilles usually hope their child will grow to embody pledge, hostage, servant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
